title: prefill/decode: chunked speculative prefill + stage-overlap + kernel scheduler improvements
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: the prefill -> decode pipeline in our runtime has increasing tail latency and suboptimal GPU utilization for mixed-length workloads. This PR implements three complementary optimizations: (1) chunked prefill (split long prefill sequences into smaller GPU-friendly chunks to reduce peak memory and improve kernel locality), (2) speculative prefill (start decode stage earlier by issuing speculative KV-cache extrapolation for likely next positions), and (3) stage overlap with an improved kernel scheduler that better balances prefill and decode kernels across available SMs/queues. The combination reduces end-to-end latency for many production workloads and increases throughput in continuous-batching scenarios.

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Can you explain how chunk boundaries are selected? Is it based on attention context windows or token count? Concern: could introduce extra copies for some tensor layouts.
Maya Chen: Chunk boundaries are set by token count but adjusted for prefix KV-cache alignment. We avoid copies by reusing KV views where possible; doc updated with explanation.
Leo Ramirez: I saw a 10-15% regression on short prompt cases in the first benchmark run. Was that transient?
Maya Chen: That was due to an aggressive speculation timeout; I tuned the threshold and added a fallback path — benchmarks re-run and regression disappears for short sequences.
Sofia Martinez: Please add tracing for kernel queue placement so we can drive future autoscaling rules.
Maya Chen: Added tracepoints and an end-to-end perf dashboard config in tools/perf.
Arjun Patel: Nit: rename speculative_patch -> speculative_prefill to be consistent with naming across runtime modules.
Maya Chen: Renamed in the last commit.
benchmarks_summary: End-to-end perf (measured on p4d-like nodes, mixed-length workloads): p50 latency -18% (from 42ms to 34.5ms), p95 latency -30% (from 120ms to 84ms), throughput +22% for continuous batching (batch sizes 8-32). Memory working set reduced ~12% for long-prefill scenarios due to chunking and early GC of KV slices. Kernel occupancy improved with the scheduler, reducing idle SM time by ~17%.
notes_on_safety_and_rollback: Speculative prefill is guarded by runtime feature gate and feature flags per-deployment. We added a per-request telemetry flag to detect extra mismatches and automatic fallback to conservative path if mismatch rate > 0.1% in a 5m window. Rollback is a config flip that disables speculative path and stage overlap scheduling.
release_notes: Performance: significant prefill->decode latency and throughput improvements via chunked prefill, speculative prefill, and stage-overlap kernel scheduling. Added runtime feature flag 'speculative_prefill' (off by default for some Dedicated customers).
